Wondering if voat could give me some help on my first modern deck! Mostly just needing sideboard help but any suggestion would be appreciated

Hey voat! So I'm going to be dropping a bit of money on my first modern deck like the title says. I'm keeping it mono red for now (but will probably add white later on). I'm mostly needin help with the sideboard but I'm also thinking of getting rid of grim lavamancer and 1 shard volley. I'm just afraid of trashing too many of my own lands but I'm not sure what to add x3 of. Any advice is much appreciated.

Hey, welcome to Modern! I am not a burn player, but I'll see how I can help.

I think this is a nice list to start with. You already stated you had a plan for a splash of white, but have you considered a splash of green for Destructive Revelry or Atarka's Command? Revelry is great in the sideboard for taking care of pesky enchantments or artifacts in Twin and Robots respectively. Command is great mainboard with the spash for basically every option but the land one (and even then, its used rarely. Ex. Triggering Landfall on Searing Blaze).If you don't want a green splash, at the least Smash to Smithereens can help deal with robots. When you add the white splash, Deflecting Palm can be used against stompy decks in the side. It stops damage, and forces their opponent to take it. Worth the casting cost.

One major sideboard card missing I noticed in mono red however is Pyroclasm. Yes, it hits your stuff, but it can halt Elves, Tokens, and Twin (Pestermite). I am an elves player. This card hurts more than any bolt ever will. Overall an amazing card, will affect the board, but only usable in certain matchups.
I'd drop Vexing Devil - it seems good, but it puts the choice on your opponent, and he'll always choose what's best for him - usually not that choice you hoped he'd make ;)
Ward! We just established /v/mtgdeckbuilding which would love submissions like yours. Come on over!!

So it looks like you got some really good advice on cards and other sources to compare sideboards. The only other thing I could add is knowing what kind of sideboard you want. Are you looking to take this to a large event? Or do you have a specific meta for Friday night magic? Most of the suggestions are good for big tournaments where you match ups will be unknown. If you let us know your meta we can help you adjust your sideboard to better fit those decks.
